text:
maria: Heads-up — Customer 'PayFlux' on dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 opened a support ticket: sudden throughput drop and elevated 429s since ~03:00 UTC. They say steady QPS, but avg tokens/sec dropped ~45%. They can reproduce with our load generator. Escalating to runtime/SRE.
ajay: Ack. Do we have metrics? p95 latency? error counts?
maria: From customer trace: p50 ~350ms -> 420ms, p95 1.2s -> 2.3s, token throughput from 480k -> 260k tokens/min. 429s started showing around 03:05. Their requests show Retry-After sometimes.
katie: Any autoscaler events? Maybe Dedicated pool scaled down or had placement churn.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] scale-down(POOL=eu-west-1-dedicated-42) triggered at 02:58 UTC -> target_replicas 4 -> 2 after 5m cooldown.
ajay: Hmm scale-down right before issue. But customer says QPS steady. Could be noisy neighbor causing small batches -> lower effective throughput even with same QPS.
oncall-sre: Pulling batcher metrics now: continuous-batcher queue depth per-shard, scheduling quantum, and max_batch_tokens histogram.
josh: I'm seeing a spike in small-batch ratio starting 03:01 — fraction of batches with <8 tokens jumped from 6% -> 48%. That's consistent with a tenant interleaving many tiny requests.
katie: That would reduce GPU utilization drastically and increase per-token latency. Any change in max_batch_tokens or scheduler config recently?
ajay: Recent deploy at 01:50 bumped scheduler quantum from 50ms -> 30ms to reduce tail latency for small requests. Could have reduced coalescing window and increased small batches.
maria: Customer reproduction steps they sent: run this loop with 1-2 token prompts at 200 qps for 5m -> see server-level 429 and latency climb. They also recorded request-ids: req-9e7f... req-9e80...
josh: Share of noisy tenant traffic also spiked from another customer (internal tenant id t-77). They had a sudden microburst of tiny completions at 03:00.
ajay: Quick mitigation options: 1) Revert scheduler quantum change in canary; 2) Increase max_batch_tokens clamp so scheduler can accept larger coalesced batches; 3) Apply per-tenant token rate limit to noisy tenant; 4) Temporarily pin PayFlux to their own dedicated GPU shard.
oncall-sre: We can try a config tweak: scheduler quantum back to 50ms on one canary host in pool-42. Low-risk.
katie: Also check continuous-batcher's prefix cache behavior — if prefixes frequently miss, we might be issuing more small forward passes.
maria: Customer wants a quick fix. They prefer we try scheduler quantum revert and watch.
ajay: I'll push canary scheduler config to 1 host in pool-42:
```
PATCH /api/v1/configs/scheduler
{"pool":"eu-west-1-dedicated-42","quantum_ms":50}
```
Deploying to host-7 canary now.
oncall-sre: Deploy done to host-7 at 03:18 UTC. Observability: host-7 batch size median jumped from 7 -> 22 after change.
josh: Host-7 token throughput recovered ~+38% and p95 on that host dropped 800ms.
katie: Nice. What's effect at pool level?
ajay: Pool-level improvement partial: pool token throughput +12% and p95 down 200ms. Noisy tenant still spreading load across hosts.
maria: Customer confirmed their load test latency improved in the canary window but still sees elevated 429s outside.
oncall-sre: Next steps: ramp canary to 30% of pool, and schedule tenant-specific throttles for t-77 if ramp doesn't contain. Also run a small migration to move PayFlux's allocations to smaller-number-of-hosts pinning.
ajay: Also filing a quick postmortem item — deploy checklist should note quantum changes and run synthetic small-prompt stress test against dedicated pools before rolling.
maria: I'll relay status to PayFlux: we rolled a canary, saw partial recovery, ramping to 30% next 20m; we'll open short maintenance if needed.
josh: For debugging record: sampling of logs from 03:04 — 03:10:
```
[03:05:12] batcher: created batch id=bd-123 size=3 tokens=12 shard=5
[03:05:12] scheduler: scheduled batch=bd-123 delay=18ms quantum=30ms
[03:06:02] cohort: tenant=t-77 requests=2200 small_requests=92%
[03:06:05] runtime: token_forward exec_time=12ms gpu_util=22%
[03:07:11] quota: emit 429 req=req-9e7f tenant=payflux reason=burst_control
```
katie: Can we also add a short-term heuristic: if small-batch fraction >40% then temporarily increase quantum up to 80ms to allow coalescing? Might help pools under noisy-tenant microbursts.
ajay: Possible — need simulation. I'll prototype a PID for quantum in the scheduler.
oncall-sre: Action items:
- ajay: ramp canary to 30% and monitor (15m)
- josh: identify top noisy tenant (t-77) and propose per-tenant throttle (10m)
- katie: run prefix-cache heatmap and check miss rate (20m)
- maria: update PayFlux & CS (5m)
- infra-bot: create incident with links to dashboards
maria: Thanks team. Will follow-up after 30m ramp. :thumbsup:
